//: No LAN address is hard-coded here. One used to be, and Kestrel fails on any machine that does not happen to own it - SocketException 10049, 'The requested address is not valid in its context' - which is every machine but the one it was written on. Use the LAN profiles below to reach the app from a phone or a headset.
//iis: This app is a standalone Blazor WebAssembly project and is run by its own host: dotnet run, or one of the four profiles below. There is no IIS Express profile and no iisSettings block, which the template left here and nothing ever used - Playwright and .claude/launch.json both pass --no-launch-profile and pin the port themselves. They were also a second web-server registration beside the self-host one, which is what Visual Studio was complaining about with "An element with the same key but a different value already exists. Key: Microsoft.WebTools.ProjectSystem.WebServer.SelfHostWebServer".

http (LAN).//: Listens on every interface, so a phone or headset on the same network can reach it at http://<this machine's IP>:5105 - whatever that address happens to be. No browser is launched, since 0.0.0.0 is not somewhere to browse to.

https (LAN).//: The same over HTTPS, which is what WebXR needs on a headset: an XR session is refused on an insecure origin unless it is localhost. Expect a certificate warning, since the dev certificate is issued for localhost rather than for this machine's address.
